title: The Odyssey, Homer
subtitle: 8th century BC AD
subject: litterature
description: After Troy, the king of Ithaca, Odysseus, took ten years to return home. Monsters, gods and temptations punctuate this journey which invents the cunning hero of Western literature.

hero.hook: Ten years to return home: literature's greatest journey home.

blocks.text: Around the **8th century BC**, a long Greek poem tells of the return of a man. This man's name is **Ulysses**, king of the small island of **Ithaca**, off the coast of Greece. In Greek, we say *Odysseus*. The **Trojan War** ended ten years ago. It was a legendary conflict between Greeks and Trojans for Queen Helena. His companions want to return. But the journey still lasts **ten years**. This is the **Odyssey**, the other great pillar of European culture, alongside the Iliad.

Here, we no longer only sing about the fury of arms. We follow a hero who survives through **cunning**, Greek *mètis*, language and endurance. To return, Ulysses will sometimes have to accept not being “**Nobody**”. In Greek, we say *Outis*. This password saves his companions against the Cyclops. The Odyssey thus invents the journey as an inner test, not just as an adventure.

sections.title: Homer, or how we sang before writing

blocks.text: The poem is attributed to **Homer**, a semi-legendary figure about whom we know almost nothing with certainty. Was it a single poet, or the name of a long tradition? Modern research, with , an American philologist of the 20th century, shows that the text comes mainly from a . For centuries,  composed live. These poet-singers improvised to the accompaniment of a lyre. They used ready-made s: “Ulysses of a Thousand Tricks”, “Rose-Fingered Dawn”. These repeated formulas made memorization and composition easier. [[Milman Parry]] [[oral tradition]] [[aedes]] [[Homeric formula]]
In Greek, the name *Homeros* can evoke “he who does not see”. Hence the legend of a blind poet going from city to city, carrying the epic in his memory rather than on a scroll.

The epic has approximately **12, 000 pours** in and **24 songs**. [[Homeric Greek]] is an archaic literary language, never spoken as it is. The verse used is the **[[dactyl]]ic hexameter**, a verse six feet long. It is punctuated by, metric units which imitate the gallop. Once written, the poem establishes an artificial language which gives the story a sacred, timeless air. This is what we call the [[The Homeric Question]]: a single author, or a collective tradition established late?

The story begins . The Latin expression means “in the middle of things”. Ulysses is held by the nymph **Calypso**, goddess who welcomes him to her island. The famous adventures then arrive in flashback. It's a [[in media res]], a flashback in the story. The hero tells them to the **Phaeacians**, welcoming people who escort him to Ithaca. The warrior becomes the storyteller of his own legend. [[analepsis]]

blocks.caption: Ulysses facing the Cyclops Polyphemus, on an ancient Greek vase.

blocks.text: Everything changes after **Cyclops Polyphemus**. He is a one-eyed giant, son of the god Poseidon. To save his men, Ulysses blinds him, then shouts his real name. **Poseidon**, god of the sea and father of the giant, then pursues him across all the seas. Among the **Lotophagous**, he rescues his companions from oblivion caused by an intoxicating plant. At **Circé**, a magician who transforms men into beasts, he gives them human form. Each step tests the **hospitality**, the *xenia*, fundamental value of the ancient Greek world. The [[nekya]], the descent into Hell to question the dead, confronts him with his own limit: speaking to the shadows, accepting what is lost.

sections.title: Ithaca: the return and the bed of olive

blocks.text: Meanwhile, in Ithaca, Queen **Penelope**, faithful wife of Odysseus, resists the **suits**. A hundred nobles pillage the palace hoping to marry her. She promises to remarry when the shroud of **Laertes**, Ulysses' father-in-law, is finished, then undoes it every night. It is feminine ruse, mirroring that of the hero.

blocks.caption: Penelope weaving the day, unmaking the night: gaining time against the suitors.

blocks.text: Ulysses is recognized first by his old dog **Argos**, then by his nurse **Eurycleia**, before Penelope tests him with the secret of their bed, carved from a living olive tree. This intimate detail proves that he is indeed the king, not an imposter.

Disguised as a beggar thanks to **Athena**, goddess of wisdom and protector of Ulysses, the hero observes, then strikes. The archery competition remains famous: only Ulysses can string the king's bow. Then came the massacre of the suitors and the restoration of order in the palace. The **nostos**, the return home, is not only a geographical journey. Home is not a house: it is a bond that we prove, an identity that we reconquer.

sections.title: Why Ulysses still speaks to us

blocks.text: Odysseus is not an invincible demigod like **Achilles**. His weapon is adaptation. He accepts humiliation, lies when necessary, cries, doubts. In the 20th century,  transposed this wandering into a single day in Dublin with his novel **Ulysses**, published in 1922. From the poet **Bellay** to “Happy is he like Ulysses…” in the cinema, the castaway who searches for his homeland remains a driving force in the story. The Odyssey asks a simple question: is it better to have immortality without risk, or a human life, fragile and chosen? [[James Joyce]]

blocks.text: The **Odyssey** invents the hero who returns home through cunning and endurance. The goal of the journey is not the immortality promised by Calypso, but a human life, fragile and chosen, found in Ithaca.
